subject.title: Cron sessions deliver hallucinated output instead of failing cleanly when tool calls fail

question: What should OpenClaw do by default when an unattended cron run has failed or missing tool evidence but then produces success-looking final assistant text?
rationale: The choice changes a security-sensitive delivery boundary and can alter existing cron announce behavior, so automation should not invent the default policy.

options.title: Core fail-closed cron finalization
options.body: Treat unsupported final assistant text after failed or missing required tool evidence as a cron failure unless structured recovery or verified delivery evidence exists.

options.title: Plugin-only claim verification
options.body: Keep broad success-claim detection outside core and only add minimal core signals needed for plugins to enforce stricter delivery policy.

options.title: Keep current recovery semantics
options.body: Preserve current final-text recovery behavior and document operator workarounds, accepting that unattended jobs may still deliver unsupported prose after some tool failures.

recommendation.title: Core fail-closed cron finalization
recommendation.body: Treat unsupported final assistant text after failed or missing required tool evidence as a cron failure unless structured recovery or verified delivery evidence exists.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current source and product-scope history for the cron/failure-signal boundary and made the adjacent ClawHub scope call.
